messages:
zoe (eng-platform): heads up — we started seeing a small but consistent stream of failures from the functions/tool-calling layer. 422s with "schema validation failed" when routed through the eu-west adapter. stack trace in logs shows the runtime rejecting the payload.
mike (eng-runtime): can you paste the failing request sample? is this new validation logic in the adapter or in the runtime schema validator?
zoe (eng-platform): here's the sanitized payload that failed (from proxy logs):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-l1",
  "input": "Generate invoice lines",
  "tools": [{"name": "create_invoice", "args_schema": {"type": "object"}}],
  "function_response": {"items": [{"line": "1 x widget", "amt": 19.99}]}
}
```
Error message: `ValidationError: function_response does not conform to declared tool schema (missing top-level fields)` — but interestingly, raw runtime logs earlier show the exact same payload validated fine when routed directly to prod-us.
mike (eng-runtime): that matches what I saw in traces. eu-west adapter strips top-level `tools` metadata when it proxies to multi-tenant runtime — so the validator at the runtime sees no declared tool schema, falls back to strict output-schema enforcement and rejects. basically a routing-induced drop.
anya (product): important: this is a UX problem too. Console shows a generic 422 for the call and a request id, but no structured info about which field failed or that the schema was missing. users are opening support tickets. we should show `schema_errors` and the tool name in the call details.
sam (eng-platform): agree on telemetry. proposal: add a counter `tool_schema_rejects_total` tagged by `route`, `adapter`, `model`, `tool_name`, and `error_kind` (missing_schema|mismatch|parse_error). then a histogram for validation latency. that will help correlate routing -> validation issues.
lisa (eng-sre): what's the blast radius? how many requests and failure rate? can we safely hotfix the adapter to stop dropping `tools` without a deploy window? we should also consider a graceful fallback: if declared schema missing, runtime should accept with a `warning` not hard 422 until we patch adapters.
zoe (eng-platform): quick numbers: ~0.6% of function invocations from eu-west in the last 6h, small but steady. support reports 8 customers affected. i'll open a ticket. agree we need both short-term runtime leniency and a medium-term adapter fix.
mike (eng-runtime): short-term patch: runtime can accept missing `tools` if request has `X-Route-Adapter: eu-west-proxy` header and emit a `schema_warning` in response body and telemetry. change is tiny, can ship in a canary today.
anya (product): console change: show `schema_warning` with expandable diff and link to request id. also surface recommended remediation text: "ensure your client includes tool declarations or route through the model-specific endpoint". product can mock the UX if you want the API shape.
sam (eng-platform): action items I can pick up: (1) add the prometheus metric and dashboard panel for `tool_schema_rejects_total` by route, (2) file infra PR to stop adapter from dropping `tools` — might require routing-layer test, (3) create alert if rate > 0.5% for > 30m in eu-west. assigning to me for (1) and (2) pairing with @mike.
mike (eng-runtime): I'll draft the runtime leniency canary and the response shape: add optional `schema_warnings` array to the tool-call response: `[{"tool": "create_invoice", "warning": "missing_declared_schema"}]`. will run it on canary and ping deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: runtime/canary v2026.3.1 -> 2 hosts in eu-west. CI: passed.
lisa (eng-sre): after canary up, we should run synthetic tool-call tests hitting eu-west and verify failure rate drops to 0 and warnings show up in payloads.
zoe (eng-platform): thanks all. i've created ticket INF-4291 with links to logs and a short postmortem template. next steps: sam + mike do the infra+runtime fixes, anya + product mock the console UX for `schema_warnings`, lisa will run SRE validation. i'll follow up in the ticket with customer IDs to reach out. :thumbsup:
